title: Swe mid scenario race condition
question: Two requests hit 'redeem coupon' for the same user at nearly the same instant. How do you make sure the coupon only gets redeemed once?
idealAnswer:
The naive check-then-act (read 'not used', then write 'used') has a race window, both requests can read 'not used' before either writes, both succeed

Fix with a database-level unique constraint (e.g. a unique index on user_id+coupon_id in a redemptions table) and let the second insert fail, rather than trying to prevent the race in application code

Alternative: an atomic conditional update (UPDATE ... WHERE used = false, check rows affected) instead of separate read-then-write steps

A strong answer explicitly identifies this as a race condition / concurrency bug, not just a logic bug, and reaches for a database-enforced guarantee rather than an application-level lock or check that can't actually be atomic across two requests

Bonus: mentioning that a distributed lock (Redis-based) is also a valid solution family, though it's more operationally complex than a unique constraint for a same-database case like this
